newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Tamil party cries foul over MP's killing.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Tamil party cries foul over MP's killing.

text.p: A moderate Tamil political party on Monday said its enemies want to silence the party by killing its leaders.
Murugesu Sivasithambaram, leader of the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), made the charge after the killing of one of its parliament deputies on Saturday.
"At this moment, I have no basis for suspecting anybody," Sivasithambaram told Reuters.
"But we have too many enemies in this country, both among the majority (Sinhalese) community and among the (minority) Tamils," he said.
TULF lawmaker Arunasalam Thangathurai and four others were killed in a grenade attack in the eastern port city of Trincomalee. Fifteen others were wounded.
Thangathurai was the eighth TULF leader to be killed since the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels gunned down the party's former leader Appapillai Amirthalingam in 1989.

"It is clear that someone would like to eliminate as many leaders as possible of the TULF, which is the only non-militant Tamil force that is functioning in the country right now," Sivasithambaram said.
Police have blamed the LTTE for the killing.
The LTTE's spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment, but he told Reuters on Saturday that he had no information about the incident.
The TULF, which has five seats in Sri Lanka's 225-seat parliament, supports the ruling People's Alliance government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga.

It has also called upon the government and the LTTE to stop fighting and initiate third party mediation for a negotiated settlement to the country's bloody ethnic conflict, which the government says has killed more than 50,000 people.
The LTTE, who are fighting for an independent homeland for Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, say the toll is higher.
Tamils constitute about 13 percent of Sri Lanka's population of 18 million and say they are being discriminated against by the Sinhalese, who make up 74 percent of the population.
Sivasithambaram said the killing of Thangathurai sent distressing signals.
"I am not only saddened, I also don't know what to do. If this is what happens to politicians in this country, you have to wonder whether doing politics is worth the while," he said.
Government forces are currently engaged in an offensive against the LTTE's northern Wanni stronghold, in a bid to open a strategic highway through the region.
The rebels say the offensive has been stalled due to heavy casualties suffered by the military from two rebel attacks.
